MixSIAR's own fits of the example data

Source: R/compare.R
mixsiar_reference.Rd

MixSIAR 3.1.12 fits of the killer whale, geese and wolves vignettes, made for benchmarking MixSIARPFN: 1,000 posterior draws of every diet proportion (thinned from the saved chains), MixSIAR's summary statistics table (which also covers the random-effect SDs and residual multipliers, whose draws were not saved), and the run settings (chain length, burn-in, run time, largest Gelman-Rubin diagnostic).

Usage

mixsiar_reference(vignette = c("killerwhale", "geese", "wolves"))

Arguments

vignette

"killerwhale", "geese" or "wolves".

Value

A list with draws (data frame: name, value; names as in MixSIAR's summary, e.g. p.Pack 1.Deer), summary (data frame: name, mean, sd, q2.5, q97.5), info (list) and ppc (list: stats, one row per checked statistic with the observed value, the replicated mean and 95% interval and the posterior predictive p-value ppp; summary and controls, how many group statistics fall outside 95% and 99% of their replicates; grouping, the factor checked).

Details

Also a posterior predictive check of each MixSIAR fit: MixSIAR's own model, rerun with replicated consumers drawn from its likelihood, compared with the data group by group (each tracer's mean and SD, and the correlation between tracers), on the standardised tracer scale MixSIAR's JAGS model uses. The same check on six datasets simulated from the model itself, like geese and like wolves, shows what a good fit looks like.
